sections.skill: Tell a chatbot, a fixed workflow and an agent apart

questions.prompt: What does a chatbot do?

choices.text: Answers in a conversation while you decide what to do
Takes actions in the world on its own, such as sending emails and buying things for you

questions.correct_answer: Answers in a conversation while you decide what to do
questions.intro: Three setups are often all called "AI," but they differ in who decides the steps. A CHATBOT answers in a conversation; you read the reply and decide what to do. A TOOL-USING WORKFLOW follows FIXED steps that a person designed, using a model for some steps, for example "when a form arrives, summarize it, then email the summary to the manager." An AGENT is given a GOAL and TOOLS (such as search, email or files) and CHOOSES its own next steps, checking results as it goes. More freedom to choose means more ways to go wrong, so agents need the most limits and oversight.

sections.skill: Compare the three with a GPS, a delivery route and a personal assistant

questions.prompt: A GPS you ask for directions is like what?
questions.intro: A GPS that you ASK for directions is like a chatbot: it suggests, and you drive. A delivery company's FIXED ROUTE, same stops in the same order every day, is like a workflow: designed in advance. A PERSONAL ASSISTANT told "get me to the airport by 6" who chooses taxis, trains and timing is like an agent: given a goal, choosing steps. The assistant is most flexible, and also the one whose choices you most need to check.

sections.skill: Look past labels to what a system can do

questions.prompt: A product is marketed as an "agent" but always runs the same three steps. What is it really?
questions.intro: Labels in product marketing are loose: something sold as an "agent" may be a fixed workflow, and a chatbot may quietly use tools such as search. Ask practical questions instead. Who decides the next step, a person, a fixed design or the model? What can it actually do in the world: only show text, or also send, buy, delete or post? Can it act without a person approving? The answers tell you how much checking and how many limits it needs.

questions.prompt: Which question best reveals the risk of a system?

choices.text: "Does it have a friendly name and a nice logo that customers will remember easily?"
"Can it act without a person approving?"
